lines.text: Three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one. Powers of three grow fast!
lines.caption: Three, nine, twenty-seven, eighty-one. Powers of three grow fast!

lines.text: Can one end in zero one?
lines.caption: Can one end in zero one?

lines.text: What is the smallest n, so three to the n ends in zero one?
lines.caption: What is the smallest n, so three to the n ends in zero one?

lines.text: The last digit loops: three, nine, seven, one. So only every fourth power ends in one.
lines.caption: The last digit loops: three, nine, seven, one. So only every fourth power ends in one.

lines.text: Three to the fourth is eighty-one. Four powers later, the tens digit drops by two.
lines.caption: Three to the fourth is eighty-one. Four powers later, the tens digit drops by two.

lines.text: Sixty-one, forty-one, twenty-one, and then zero one!
lines.caption: Sixty-one, forty-one, twenty-one, and then zero one!

lines.text: Five jumps of four powers. So n is twenty!
lines.caption: Five jumps of four powers. So n is twenty!

lines.text: Check: three to the twentieth ends in zero one.
lines.caption: Check: three to the twentieth ends in zero one.

lines.text: Why does it drop? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
lines.caption: Why does it drop? The full lesson shows two ways, plus every trap.
